newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Mauritania government projects balanced '97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Mauritania government projects balanced '97 budget.

text.p: Mauritania's government has drafted a 1997 budget which projects an increase of over seven percent on 1996 but aims to balance the books for a second successive year, officials said.

The draft, approved by the government earlier this week and submitted to the national assembly, projects a budget of 46.470 billion ouguiyas ($331.5 million) compared to 43.188 billion ouguiyas for 1996, the officials added.

Central Bank officials said in October that in 1996 the West African nation, which forms a link between black and Arab Africa, was heading for its first budget surplus since independence from France in 1960.
Officials said that the 1997 budget draft projected a 7.17 percent increase in government receipts and a six percent increase in spending with budgetary rigour once again the watchword.
Education, health and the fight against poverty were the spending priorities, they added.

It was not immediately clear when parliament would debate the draft but supporters of President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya in the ruling Democratic and Social Republican Party won a landslide victory in October's parliamentary election.
Officials said that the debate was likely to take place early in December. ($1 = 140.185 Mauritania ouguiyas)
